adversarial_trace.step1: t = |W| - 867 <= 4; by the fixed-representative reduction W may be taken to be its own fixed representative
adversarial_trace.step2: its coordinate vector satisfies the row constraints, so it is one of the 1,609 rows at t <= 4
adversarial_trace.step3: by Claim 1 its chains carry exactly 120 + G - 5c ports
adversarial_trace.step4: by H.catalogue_complete + H.charging_rules + H.start_wlog those chains are walks in the transition system, and by H.extraction_budgets their resources are inside the row's budgets
adversarial_trace.step5: for every row at t <= 4 except two, the computed maximum over such walks is STRICTLY below the required port count -- contradiction
adversarial_trace.step6: for the two equality rows the maximum equals the requirement, so the chains must ATTAIN it; the equality witnesses were enumerated exhaustively twice, once with no pruning table
adversarial_trace.step7: the incidence equality then forces the tree condition, all 120 hexagons used, and c pure circuits covering F with |F| = 4c; three independent solvers with positive controls show no such c orbits exist -- contradiction
adversarial_trace.which_lemma_must_break: H.catalogue_complete or H.charging_rules: the cover's chain would have to use a joint outside the catalogue, or charge less than the rules say.  Both are closed by finite enumeration, not by sampling.
